In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
structures need to be designed to withstand the effects of the earthquake ground motions that may be encountered during their design life.
the design of buildings in seismic areas should be based on the most severe ground motion that can reasonably be expected in that area.
structures should be designed with consideration for a wide variety of ground motions, including near fault ground motions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
structures should be designed for a larger earthquake than the design earthquake and should be able to withstand the earthquake without significant damage.

the design and analysis of structures should be done in a manner that is consistent with the design code and with a proper understanding of the seismic design implications of the selected ground motions.
the seismic design of structures should take into account not only ground motion intensity but also ground motion characteristics and the structural response characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of structures needs to be based on realistic ground motions and not on design spectra.
the design of structures for earthquakes is not a one-size fits all approach.
structures should be designed to withstand the maximum expected ground motions, and not to the maximum recorded ground motions.
